title: The Great Roll
summary: The word of the Lord instructs the narrator to take a great roll and write concerning Maher-shalal-hash-baz. The narrator reports taking Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah as faithful witnesses to record.

explicit_facts.text: The word of the Lord instructs the narrator to take a great roll and write in it with a man’s pen concerning Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
The narrator reports taking faithful witnesses to record: Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah.

The roll’s dimensions and material and the pen’s appearance are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Take thee a great roll, and write in it with a man’s pen, concerning Maher-shalal-hash-baz.

narration.text: And I took unto me faithful witnesses to record, Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi is the narrator label supplied by the user; these verses themselves identify the narrator only through first-person pronouns.

title: The Child Is Named
summary: The narrator reports going to the prophetess, who conceived and bore a son. The Lord instructs him to name the child Maher-shalal-hash-baz and foretells the taking of Damascus’s riches and Samaria’s spoil before the child can cry for his father and mother.

explicit_facts.text: The narrator reports going to the prophetess, who conceived and bore a son.
The Lord tells the narrator to call the child Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
The Lord foretells that the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria will be taken away before the king of Assyria before the child knows how to cry for his father and mother.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The naming instruction can be presented with the narrator listening, without depicting the Lord.

The setting of the naming instruction
Whether the prophetess and child are present during the instruction

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The supplied task identifies the first-person narrator as Nephi; these verses themselves do not name him. The character label follows that instruction.

Do not depict the predicted taking of riches and spoil as occurring here.

Do not place the king of Assyria physically in the scene.
